name: Ponderosa Pines
award: 2025 Federal 4% and noncompetitive state housing tax credits
headline: Ulysses Development Group is building Ponderosa Pines, 204 new one- to three-bedroom apartments for households averaging 60% AMI, at Scott Avenue and Parker Road on the Parker side of unincorporated Douglas County. It won a 2025 federal 4% credit award plus noncompetitive state credit from CHFA, with Douglas County Housing Partnership as bond issuer.
why_it_matters: This is the same developer's Scott Avenue workforce-housing site, which the county Planning Commission rejected and neighbors sued over in 2023 (inferred to be the same site). It shows a contested suburban rezoning carried through to a closed deal by stacking DCHP bonds, recycled CHFA bonds, a Prop 123 loan and county More Housing Now money.

status.label: Financing closed and groundbreaking held (September 2026); under construction per developer
status.detail: Mile High CRE reported the financial close on 2026-09-14 and the groundbreaking ceremony on 2026-09-30, and the developer's project page lists the deal as closed in September 2026 and under construction. Completion is targeted for 2028.

next_step: Watch for Douglas County building permits and construction progress, and lease-up with a Douglas County employment preference in 2028.

background.text: In February 2023 BusinessDen reported that Ulysses planned 220 workforce apartments on 35 acres at State Highway 83 (Parker Road) and Scott Avenue; the county Planning Commission voted 8-0 to deny it on 2022-12-19, the county commissioners approved it 2-1, and 106 Pinery-area residents sued. This is inferred to be the Ponderosa Pines site, given the matching corner and developer.
The developer described the project as a five-year effort, including getting the site rezoned for multifamily.

The state announced a preliminary $6M Prop 123 concessionary debt award on 2025-07-30, one of six awards totaling $27,053,646; final terms were left to underwriting. The amount reported at closing was $4.35M.

The county commissioners took up the TEFRA resolution for up to $50M of DCHP bonds at their 2026-08-25 business meeting; the county said bonds will finance at least 25% of aggregate basis to qualify for the 4% credit.
No public document found shows the deal in CHFA's 2025 competitive rounds.

discrepancies.text: CHFA prints the address as 6793 Scott Avenue, while the closing and groundbreaking articles give 6010 Pinery Center Blvd.
CHFA lists one- to three-bedroom units only, while the groundbreaking article and Colorado Politics describe one- to four-bedroom units.
CHFA and the county's TEFRA approval put the Douglas County Housing Partnership bonds at $50M, while the closing announcement describes $27M of DCHP bonds plus $15M of recycled CHFA bonds.
The state's 2025 announcement and DCHP give a $6M Prop 123 award, while closing reports give $4.35M.
Mile High CRE reports a $180 million project, while the developer's press list cites a Colorado Real Estate Journal headline of $97 million.
CHFA lists $4,442,978 a year of federal credit (about $44.4M over 10 years) and $700,000 of state credit, while Colorado Politics reported $34.5M in federal credits and $3.36M in state credits.
News reports place the project in Parker, while the state and DCHP describe it as in unincorporated Douglas County.
